overview: Crew Duty-Rest Compliance Planning addresses alerts and control records are fragmented, delaying a defensible review of priority exceptions in aviation and airports operations. The first proof of value uses rosters, flight delays and duty limitation rules. It produces a reviewed operational recommendation and a traceable decision record. The commercial success measure is noncompliant crew duty assignments, established from customer baseline data before any improvement is claimed.

scope:
Delivery model: Redington or approved implementation partner, eligibility and staffing pending confirmation.
Duration: Discovery and design first; pilot and rollout durations depend on data access and scope; no fixed commitment.
1) Discover source quality and baseline: rosters, flight delays and duty limitation rules; define noncompliant crew duty assignments and data-processing boundary.
2) Design control points, security and connector contracts; obtain owner approval from Airport COO / Airline Operations Director.
3) Implement one bounded workflow, instrument missing-data exceptions and system-of-record write-back.
4) Test positive, negative, privilege, partial-data and rollback cases including sample false positives and adjudications with independent risk reviewers.
5) Review KPI in the pilot, document evidence, perform training and agree transition.
deliverables: Agreed test threshold for noncompliant crew duty assignments
